_doc: [OPUS-5] sparq-org/sparq#5799 — run-body failure-swallow waivers. A GitHub Actions step can be made unable to fail DECLARATIVELY (`continue-on-error:`) or IMPERATIVELY, inside the `run:` body, with `cmd || true` / `set +e`. The second form is invisible to YAML-structure checks: the step reports success, the job stays green, and `ci-summary / gate` counts a check-run that asserted nothing. scripts/check-workflow-run-swallow.py closes that hole for every job that GATES (i.e. every job NOT declared in .github/advisory-registry.json — the same load-bearing definition ci_summary_gate.py has used since #3773). W1 flags EVERY statement-level `|| true` / `|| :` in a gating job. There is NO exemption by command name: a program is not intrinsically observational — `grep -q required out.log || true`, `find . -exec validate {} \; || true` and `cat generated-artifact || true` are assertions with the verdict deleted, and a shell function named `true` is not `true(1)` — so a diagnostic `cat`/`ls`/`tail` is declared here exactly like `git`, `gh`, `npm`, `cargo`, `python3` or a repo script, with a REASON that argues why THAT invocation removes no verdict. Each entry needs {workflow, job_id, match, reason, registered}: `match` is a substring of the normalised logical command (>= 12 chars, so it pins the specific command rather than rubber-stamping the job), and W3 fails if it matches nothing live, so a waiver cannot rot into a standing pre-authorisation for a future swallow. THIS IS A RATCHET, NOT AN APPROVAL LIST: the 22 entries below are the complete set of W1-flagged sites on main as of 2026-09-02 — every `|| true` in a gating job — each one read in context and found intentional. Adding an entry is a deliberate act; removing a swallow is always preferred to declaring it. Precedent that this failure mode is real and not theoretical: the PR #4211 review found `gh issue edit --add-label "$l" || true` in triage-issue.yml silently dropping ROUTING labels when a label did not exist, leaving `status:ready` set without its paired role label — the `|| true` on that call was deleted, and the comment block above the step records why.

waivers.reason: History deepening for a regression-attribution `git log baseline..HEAD` after a shallow checkout. Both fetch spellings are tried because `--unshallow` errors on a repo that is already complete; the trailing `|| true` covers the case where neither is needed. If the history is still too shallow the attribution step downstream reports that itself, so no verdict is silenced here.

Cleanup on the failure branch of `if git fetch origin main && git rebase FETCH_HEAD`. The rebase is a best-effort retry of the perf-floor commit against a main tip that moved during the long bench job; aborting a rebase that never started is not a failure. The perf gate itself is a separate, unswallowed step.

Best-effort disk reclamation between the two attempts of the sq-c76x transient-shard self-heal, in case the first attempt was a `No space left` race that left partial extraction behind. Reclaiming zero bytes is a legitimate outcome; the retried shard's own exit code is captured and re-raised (`exit "$rc"`) two lines above, so the shard verdict is unaffected.

The cone coverage REPORT step (`--mode report`), which renders the measured cone into $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. Its own header states it never fails the shard: coverage-gate.py --check-robust, run unswallowed in the preceding step, is the sole coverage gate. A rendering failure must not red a shard whose coverage gate passed.

Lifts the one-line pass/fail tally out of the report log into $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, inside a `{ … } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` group. The verdict is the `cargo run … --bin served-conformance-report` two lines above, which runs under `set -o pipefail` with NO swallow and is the fail-closed emitter; if it produced no report there is no summary line to find, and that failure has already reddened the step. Only the cosmetic summary line is tolerated missing.

Cleanup on the `else` branch of the premerge merge probe. The non-zero merge exit is NOT swallowed — it is the signal, recorded as `merged=false` in $GITHUB_OUTPUT on the line above and branched on downstream. Aborting the merge only restores the working tree.

The anti-OOM invariant between Kani harnesses: reap any orphaned cbmc solver before the next harness starts. pkill exits 1 when there is nothing to reap, which is the expected and desired state. The harness verdict is captured separately on the line above (`&& ec=0 || ec=$?`) and acted on.

Renders the last 40 lines of a FAILED harness's log into a `<details>` block in the step summary — it sits inside `if [ "$ec" -ne 0 ]`, i.e. on a path where the failure has ALREADY been recorded (`had_fail=1` plus an `::error title=Kani proof failed::` annotation on the lines above). The harness verdict is `ec`, captured unswallowed and acted on; a truncated or missing log tail degrades the report, not the verdict.

Deliberate, documented verdict RECLASSIFICATION, not a swallow. `cargo miri nextest` exits 100 both when a heavy loader test TIMED OUT (known cost debt, sq-0s15k) and when Miri found genuine UB, and the raw code cannot tell them apart — so the lane concluded `failure` every night on tracked debt and masked whether Miri found anything. The run emits a libtest-json-plus event stream to a file, and the NEXT step ('Classify shard verdict') parses it and exits 1 on a real UB/assertion failure. That classifier step is the shard verdict and carries no swallow.

Echoes the shard's captured stderr into the log so a human reading the run can see what Miri printed. It is the FIRST line of the 'Classify shard verdict' step; the verdict is `python3 scripts/miri_classify_verdict.py --events …` on the very next line, unswallowed, and that exit code IS the shard verdict. A missing .stderr file (e.g. the shard aborted before writing it) must not pre-empt the classifier's own, more precise diagnosis.

Feeds the glob-fold assertion's `while read` loop from `git ls-tree -d origin/benchmark-data dev/ | grep -E '^dev/bench'` via process substitution. grep exits 1 when the branch carries no dev/bench* subtree — an empty worklist, which the loop already handles by asserting nothing. Bash does not propagate a process-substitution exit status to the `done <` redirection anyway, so this `|| true` is belt-and-braces under `set -euo pipefail`. STATED BOUND: it does make a grep MALFUNCTION look like an empty branch; the overlay itself (`git archive … | tar -x`) and the `[ "$missing" -eq 0 ] || exit 1` verdict below are both unswallowed, so a dropped worklist weakens this assertion's coverage without ever turning a real regression green.

Probe, not an assertion. It asks the registry whether the just-published version carries a provenance attestation; a package published WITHOUT provenance makes `npm view` exit non-zero, which is exactly the case the following lines must inspect rather than crash on under `set -euo pipefail`. The verdict is the emptiness test on $att, which fails the job unswallowed.

Same provenance-attestation probe as publish.yml:npm, for the eyereasoner-compat package. The `|| true` keeps a missing-attestation registry response from aborting under `set -euo pipefail` before the explicit emptiness check can report it.

Same provenance-attestation probe as publish.yml:npm, for the solid-server package. The `|| true` keeps a missing-attestation registry response from aborting under `set -euo pipefail` before the explicit emptiness check can report it.

Prints what the per-crate `cargo package` loop staged. The assertion is the very next statement — `if [ -z "$(ls -A crate-pkgs/ 2>/dev/null)" ]; then echo '::error::no .crate artifacts produced'; exit 1; fi` — which is unswallowed and covers the exact case (`crate-pkgs/` empty or absent) that would make this `ls -l` non-zero. Listing the directory twice must not be able to red the job before that check runs.

Diagnostics on an ALREADY-FAILING path: it sits inside `if [[ -z "$binary" ]]`, between the `ERROR: no release binary found under target/release` message and an unconditional `exit 1` on the next line. The step fails either way; the listing only tells the reader what WAS in target/release, and must not mask the exit 1 by failing first when the directory does not exist at all.

Same shape as the `ls -la target/release` waiver in this job: it is inside `if [ "$found" -eq 0 ]`, after `ERROR: tauri build produced no installer bundles under $BUNDLE_DIR` and immediately before an unconditional `exit 1`. The verdict is `found`, computed unswallowed by the staging loop above. A missing $BUNDLE_DIR is the very condition being reported, so `find` failing there is expected and must not short-circuit the explicit exit 1.

Harvests the pinned trusted-builder refs out of release.yml + dist.yml into `refs=$(…)` under `set -euo pipefail`. ZERO matches is precisely the failure this step exists to catch, and it is caught EXPLICITLY two lines below: `count` is compared against 1 and anything other than exactly one distinct ref exits 1. Without the `|| true` a zero-match grep would abort the step under errexit before that count check could emit its specific `expected exactly ONE distinct pinned ref … found 0` diagnostic.

Quarantine labelling for an untrusted author. Both labels are on ONE call, so this cannot half-apply the way the #4211 defect did; the quarantine's load-bearing half is that untrusted content is not acted on, which is enforced by the `if:` conditions on the downstream steps, not by this label write. Tolerated so a forge hiccup on a cosmetic label cannot red the triage lane. NB the ROUTING label write in the same job deliberately carries NO swallow (see the [OPUS-5] fail-closed comment block above it).

waivers.match: so the approval no longer applies
waivers.reason: Best-effort courtesy comment explaining a re-quarantine after a revision-bound approval lapsed. It is a notification; the re-quarantine itself is the label write, and a failed comment must not red the lane.

Best-effort courtesy comment explaining first-time quarantine to a non-collaborator. It is a notification; the quarantine itself is the label write plus the downstream `if:` conditions, and a failed comment must not red the lane.

This `|| true` is what makes the label create IDEMPOTENT: `gh label create` exits non-zero when the label already exists, which is the common case. It is the fix from the #4211 review, not the bug — the ensure-then-write ordering exists so the single all-or-nothing `gh issue edit` that follows cannot fail on a missing label. The function already refuses any name outside the closed role:/status:/needs: set.
